Subject: Custody guardrail and exhibit request for MSA

Vivek,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the performance profile. Procurement and legal here are trying to close the commercials but we have a couple of gating items related to private hosting (on-prem / VPC) that need to be captured in the MSA exhibits. Specifically:

- We need an "Operator custody" exhibit that defines: evidence types (snapshots, logs), frequency of snapshot escrow, authorized witnessing roles, and acceptable handback flows.
- A clear carveout for geo/jurisdictional custody and a short forensic access SLA for incident response.
- Proof of ability to provide a read-only evidence package within 72 hours in a test scenario.

Can you share a draft exhibit we can review with counsel and our security team? If you have an internal runbook or a short checklist for the evidence package, that would be helpful. We are aiming to complete legal redlines by end of next week to keep the Q3 rollout timeline.

Attachments: attachment stub (requirements_matrix.xlsx, application/xlsx)

Thanks,
Maya Rao

2) Internally we will call out: types of artifacts delivered (snapshots, compressed KV cache export, audit logs, chain-of-custody manifest), expected delivery SLA for test vs. production, witnessing options (third-party escrow, remote authenticated witness, on-site witness), and the minimum acceptance checklist for handback.
3) We'll include a short forensic access SLA (72 hours for read-only package; extended forensic work scoped separately).

David / Marissa / Rachel — can you review the technical and legal signal items below and call out anything that must be in the exhibit? From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Custody guardrail and exhibit request for MSA

Vivek — looped in our engineering/product and legal buddies below. Quick technical notes for the draft exhibit and runbook:

- Evidence types: we should enumerate (a) encrypted snapshot of model weights/config (sealed, hash-signed), (b) runtime image (container manifest + image digest), (c) KV cache dump for on-prem incidents, (d) structured audit logs (JSON) with retention windows.
- Snapshot cadence: recommended default = quarterly sealed deposit. For regulated customers offer monthly rotation as an SLA add-on.
- Delivery mechanics: provide a signed manifest and an encrypted transfer package (S3 presigned URL or secure courier for on-prem media). Include instructions for verification (SHA256) and a checksum validation step in the runbook.
- Witnessing: third-party witness (Ivan) is acceptable. Recommend: witness performs independent checksum validation and signs acceptance of the sealed snapshot.
- Test scenario: we can simulate a read-only evidence package delivery within 48 hours for a pre-agreed test type; production forensic package within 72 hours as Vivek suggested.

A couple of redline proposals for legal team to consider:
- Limit Redwood liability for evidence integrity to providing the signed manifest and transport chain verification; do not accept obligation for third-party forensic conclusions.
- Define a narrow acceptance checklist for handback to avoid protracted signoff windows (e.g., 5 business days after acceptance test signoff).

Marissa / Rachel — please add legal framing and any customer-facing acceptance language. I can draft the technical exhibit section and hand it to legal for redline.

Cheers,
David Kim
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
